Subset a peak_params object to a chosen set of samples

Source: R/peak_catalog.R
subset_peak_params.Rd

Given a peak_params object with sample_idx_raw (or after backfill_sample_idx_raw()), returns a new peak_params containing only the peaks and metadata for the specified samples. Useful for building per-condition catalogs from a single pooled estimate_peak_params run — split a combined disease+control peak_params into pp_disease and pp_control without rerunning the expensive step.

Usage

subset_peak_params(peak_params, sample_indices)

Arguments

peak_params

A peak_params object with sample_idx_raw.

sample_indices

Integer vector of sample indices (in the original peak_params' 1..n_samples space) to keep. Common pattern: which(y == disease_label).

Value

A peak_params-shaped list containing only the specified samples' peaks. Ready to pass to build_peak_catalog() and other downstream tools.

Details

Sample indices in the returned object are remapped to 1:length(sample_indices) so downstream tools that expect contiguous 1-based indexing work. Samples keep their original relative order (sample_indices is sorted). Every per-peak vector (every field ending in _raw, including rt_seconds_raw / cv_volts_raw) is subset with the same mask, and every per-sample field (sample_names, sample_cohort, time_ranges, cv_ranges, n_peaks$values, per-sample alignment vectors) is subset to the kept samples. Fitted summary statistics (rt_loc$mean/sd, sigma_rt$meanlog/sdlog, etc.) are recomputed from the subset; noise stats are kept as-is (pooled across samples in the original run, which is usually close enough unless the condition of interest has systematically different background noise).
